summary:
Season-long signals remain the trustworthy baseline here since 14-day windows are dry across the board (n=0 on every rating/category cell) — this late in the year, with the slate thin, there's simply no fresh sample to chase. What does carry forward is the SP streak: all four ratings show 3W on starting-pitcher picks, and trends+sp is still the top combo at 58% (370-268, n=638). That combo is the first filter to run on tonight's board — any game where trends and sp agree on the same side should be the headline look, especially layered with R3, which edges out the field at 58% season-wide (266-196, +92.0u) and carries the best 30-day strong-play mark at 2-1 among the pack.

On tonight's card, lean into where team trends intersect with that hot SP streak. LAD remains the premier "when liked" team at 70% straight-up and a blistering 80% on strong plays (28-7, +27.0u) — if the Dodgers show up on tonight's slate with an SP-backed strong play, that's about as clean a signal as this model produces. BOS (70%, strong 76% +19.0u) and TBR (70%, strong 70% +21.0u) sit right behind as auto-trust teams when the rating flags them. Fade NYY on sight — 49% straight-up and a brutal 39% on strong plays (-4.0u) makes it the one team where disagreement among categories should kill the play rather than embolden it. Meanwhile, every rating's bullpen_fatigue cell is stuck on a 3L skid at a sub-50% season clip (520-598, 47%) — if bullpen_fatigue is the lone category pushing a pick tonight without trends or sp backing it, treat it as a contrarian red flag, not a green light. Prioritize games where trends+sp converge on R3 or R4 (R4 still running 64% season-wide, +63.0u) and where the team side lines up with MIL, TBR, BOS, or LAD.
